title: Tests run against the production on-disk ./books.db with no isolation or cleanup
evidence: main.go:30 sql.Open("sqlite3", "./books.db"); main_test.go:30,58,78,117,167 each call initDB() and then create rows that are never deleted
suggestion: Point initDB at a path parameter (or file::memory:?cache=shared) and give each test a fresh DB with t.Cleanup

title: Repeated initDB() reassigns the global *sql.DB without closing the previous pool
evidence: main.go:28-32 initDB() assigns package-global db unconditionally; main_test.go calls it 5 times, leaking 4 connection pools per test binary
suggestion: Guard with sync.Once, or have initDB return (*sql.DB, error) so callers own the lifetime

title: GET /books encodes null instead of [] when the collection is empty
evidence: main.go:122 `var books []Book` stays nil when no rows match, and main.go:133 json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(books) emits `null`
suggestion: Initialise with `books := []Book{}` so the empty list marshals as []

title: Error responses are text/plain, not JSON
evidence: main.go:67,73,158,198,204 use http.Error(...), which writes Content-Type: text/plain even though TASK.md asks for JSON responses; only success paths set application/json
suggestion: Add a writeJSONError helper that sets application/json and encodes {"error": ...}

title: GET /books list-all and ?author= filter are implemented but never exercised by a test
evidence: getBooksHandler (main.go:95-134) has no corresponding test in main_test.go; the 6 tests cover health, create, validation, get-by-id, update, delete only — consistent with test_coverage=0.426
suggestion: Add a test that creates two books by different authors and asserts both list-all and ?author= filtering

title: ?author= filter is an unanchored substring LIKE match
evidence: main.go:109 `WHERE author LIKE ?` with main.go:110 "%"+author+"%", so ?author=o matches every author containing 'o'; user-supplied % and _ are also treated as wildcards
suggestion: Use an exact match (or document the substring behaviour) and escape LIKE metacharacters

title: {id} parsing is duplicated verbatim across three handlers instead of using a router
evidence: main.go:144-155, 182-192, 242-252 repeat the same strings.HasPrefix/TrimPrefix/Atoi block; a Go 1.22 ServeMux pattern ("GET /books/{id}") or a helper would collapse it
suggestion: Extract parseBookID(r) (int, error), or bump to Go 1.22 method+wildcard mux patterns
